verses.1:1: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our beloved and fellow worker,
verses.1:2: and to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house:
verses.1:3: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: I give thanks to my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
verses.1:5: hearing of your love and of the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,
verses.1:6: that the fellowship of your faith may become effective in the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
verses.1:7: For I have had great joy and consolation over your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
verses.1:8: Therefore, although I have much boldness in Christ to command you what is fitting,
verses.1:9: yet for love's sake I rather appeal to you, being such a one as Paul, an aged man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus—
verses.1:10: I appeal to you for my child, whom I have fathered in chains, Onesimus,
verses.1:11: who formerly was useless to you, but now is useful both to you and to me.
verses.1:12: I am sending him back to you, that is, my very heart,
verses.1:13: whom I would have wished to keep with myself, so that on your behalf he might minister to me in the chains of the gospel;
verses.1:14: but without your consent I did not wish to do anything, so that your goodness might not be as by compulsion, but of your own free will.
verses.1:15: For perhaps it was for this reason that he was separated from you for a little while, that you might have him back forever,
verses.1:16: no longer as a bondservant, but more than a bondservant, a beloved brother—especially to me, yet how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
verses.1:17: Therefore, if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
verses.1:18: And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
verses.1:19: I, Paul, have written this with my own hand: I myself will repay it—lest I should say to you that you owe me your very self as well.
verses.1:20: Yes, brother, may I have benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
verses.1:21: Being confident of your obedience, I have written to you, knowing that you will do even beyond what I say.
verses.1:22: At the same time, prepare a lodging for me also, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be graciously granted to you.
verses.1:23: Epaphras, my fellow captive in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
verses.1:24: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
verses.1:25: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

notes.1:6: "Fellowship" translates Greek koinonia (also "sharing" or "participation"). The Greek critical text reads "in us" (en hemin), whereas some later manuscripts read "in you."
notes.1:9: "An aged man" translates Greek presbytes, though some interpreters take it as a spelling variant of presbeutes ("an ambassador").
notes.1:11: Paul plays on the name Onesimus, which means "useful" or "profitable," contrasting "useless" (achrestos) with "useful" (euchrestos); a similar wordplay recurs in verse 20 with "may I have benefit" (onaimen).
notes.1:16: "Bondservant" translates Greek doulos ("slave"), reflecting Onesimus's legal status as well as his transformed standing as a brother in Christ.
